title: Olive and Poppyseed's Soft Surprise
markdown:
The moonbeams kissed the windowpanes and laid slivers of silver on the floor. The wide world grew very, very quiet. In a little warm cottage, Olive the otter and Poppyseed the pony were getting ready for cozy sleep.

Olive loved to wiggle her nose when she was happy. Tonight she was happy. Her fur was the colour of warm wet river pebbles. Her paws were wonderfully gentle. Poppyseed’s mane was like spun moonlight. Her hooves made soft little thumps, a quiet song on the ground.

Olive blinked her big round eyes.

“Poppyseed,” she whispered, soft as a summer leaf. “Look what I found.”

On the little wooden porch a sleepy lavender bush nodded its purple head. Beside it lay a tiny bundle. Not a toy. A bundle of the softest warmest feathers, pale in the moonlight. They looked like a little warm hug. They were not in their right place.

Poppyseed lowered her long kind head. “Oh my. They look like they need to be home.”

Olive’s nose gave the smallest wiggle. “Yes. But we must be careful. They are so light. We must not ruffle even one.”

She wanted to scoop them up and run. But the feathers were lighter than breath. Therefore she only nudged the bundle with her soft nose. The feathers felt like warm whispers.

Poppyseed might have given a bigger push. But the bundle might scatter. Therefore she lowered her nose too, and they nudged together, making a little pillow of warmth.

Olive lifted it with her most careful paws. It felt like a piece of cloud. Poppyseed walked beside her. Thump. Thump. A lullaby for the sleeping world. They saw flowers tucking in their petals. They heard crickets settling into tiny chirps.

“So soft,” Olive hummed.

“So peaceful,” Poppyseed whispered.

They walked toward the little wren nest on the porch — twigs and green moss, a tiny cozy bed. The lavender nodded them along. Olive meant to set the feathers down at once. But a night breeze lifted one edge. Therefore they paused, and Olive waited until the air was still, and Poppyseed stood like a moonlit wall against the wind, and then Olive placed the bundle in the very middle.

The feathers nestled. They looked ready to keep a wren family extra warm. A sleepy wren stirred and let out a tiny happy peep. Everything was just right.

Olive and Poppyseed looked at each other. Their hearts felt warm. They turned, with soft thumps and gentle wiggles, and went back inside.

They curled into their own beds, under their own cozy blankets. Olive yawned a tiny yawn. Poppyseed sighed. The moonlight tucked them in. The world was quiet.

Soon Olive and Poppyseed were asleep, dreaming of soft feathers and silvery light, the porch nest safe, the lavender still nodding.
